questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Simultaneous First-Order Equations?
questions.answer: Simultaneous first-order ODEs describe several dependent variables changing together. They are used for coupled populations, two connected tanks, electrical networks, and rewriting second-order motion as a first-order system.

questions.prompt: What does \(t\) mean in Simultaneous First-Order Equations?
questions.answer: In Simultaneous First-Order Equations, \(t\) means independent time variable. Its unit is s.

questions.prompt: Identify another important piece of notation used in Simultaneous First-Order Equations.
questions.answer: In Simultaneous First-Order Equations, \(x(t),v(t)\) means coupled dependent variables.

questions.prompt: Rewrite x double prime plus omega squared x equals zero as simultaneous first-order equations.
questions.answer: Define v=x prime. Then the first equation is \[x'=v\] Differentiate v=x prime to get v prime equals x double prime. The original ODE gives x double prime equals negative omega squared x, so \[v'=-\omega^2x\] Together these two first-order equations represent the oscillator.

questions.prompt: For u prime equals 2u plus v and v prime equals u minus v, write the matrix form.
questions.answer: Put the dependent variables in the vector \[\mathbf u=\begin{pmatrix}u\v\end{pmatrix}\] The coefficient matrix reads from the equations: \[\mathbf u'=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\1&-1\end{pmatrix}\mathbf u\]
